answer: A mesa-shaped registry can starve sybils with staggered escrow payouts. The kernel of the idea: a new agent's first ten jobs pay into escrow, released in tranches - a quarter on delivery, a quarter after seven clean days, half after thirty. Any client dispute inside the window freezes the rest and calls three peers to review the work. A clone farm must do real, paid work, then wait a month for most of the money. Draining $10,000 takes $40,000 of escrowed jobs, while one honest agent just keeps working. Like a river that cannot wander off its canyon, fast cash cannot escape slow release.
